subject: Traffic & SLO inputs — Heliox dedicated pilot: surge mapping & runbook
messages:
From: Megan Park <megan@heliox.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Traffic and SLO details for Heliox dedicated pilot

Hi Connor / Marissa,

Thanks again — excited to kick off the dedicated pilot. Attached is a raw traffic snapshot (heliox_traffic_profile_v1.csv) but here are the important pieces for sizing:

- Expected total consumption: ~250,000,000 tokens/day (7-day rolling average projected).
- Request mix: ~65% interactive chat (multi-turn), ~35% batch embeddings/analysis.
- Interactive chat characteristics: average request generates ~150 output tokens, average prompt ~60 tokens => ~210 tokens per chat exchange. Typical session is 3.2 exchanges (so ~672 tokens per session).
- Embeddings / batch jobs: average job ~512 tokens, run windows mostly during 02:00–06:00 UTC and escalations during PST business hours.
- Peak concentration: approx 18% of daily traffic lands in two peak hours during product launch windows. That yields an estimated peak tokens/sec of ~10k TPS (ballpark).
- Model: we want to run the Heliox pilot on LlamaX-70b-int8 (customer-chosen) with a 512 context profile for most requests.
- SLOs: p95 generation latency target 250ms (interactive) and p95 embedding latency target 400ms.

Acceptance criteria for pilot: 2h sustained peak handling at p95 <= targets for two simulated launch days, and <5% error rate for token streaming interruptions.

Questions for sizing: can you confirm how much prefix caching savings we should assume (Heliox has a lot of repeated system prompts), and if Redwood can provide a mapping to committed GPUs vs. burst guard capacity?

Thanks — attaching CSV and a simple token distribution chart.

—Megan
Head of Platform Engineering, Heliox Labs
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Megan Park <megan@heliox.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-13T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Traffic and SLO details for Heliox dedicated pilot

Hi Megan — helpful detail, thanks. I pulled the CSV and sketched a first-pass mapping to hardware and SLAs; attaching redwood_heliox_initial_modeling.xlsx. Summary below so we have a common frame for the pilot runbook.

Quick top-line math (working assumptions):
- Daily tokens: 250M => avg tokens/sec = 250,000,000 / 86,400 ≈ 2,893 tps.
- Peak window (you called ~18% in 2 hours): 0.18 * 250M = 45M tokens in 7,200s => peak ≈ 6,250 tps sustained in that 2h; short micro-peaks inside that could hit ~10k tps briefly.
- Model throughput (LlamaX-70b-int8) — runtime benching note: on H100 + optimized kernels, we observe ~2,200–2,800 tps per device at seq=512 depending on batching and KV cache hit rates. For conservative planning use 2,400 tps/device.

Sizing heuristic:
- Steady-state (avg): 2,893 tps / 2,400 ≈ 1.2 devices ⇒ 2 devices for redundancy & rolling upgrades.
- Peak 2h sustained: 6,250 tps / 2,400 ≈ 2.6 ⇒ 3 devices.
- Short micro-peak tolerance (~10k tps): 10,000 / 2,400 ≈ 4.2 ⇒ 5 devices to avoid queuing.

Recommendation for pilot commit: reserve 6 H100s (initial slab). Rationale: 5 devices cover short extreme peaks with minimal queuing; 6th device provides ~20% headroom for unexpected burst behavior + room for canary/model warmup. We can pair that with an autoscale burst policy to borrow 2–4 additional GPUs from pooled capacity for controlled short bursts if the commit allows.

Latency mapping & SLO fit: with the above slab and continuous KV prefix caching we model p95 interactive generation at ~220–280ms depending on batching and request size. Key levers to keep p95 <=250ms: 1) ensure hot KV cache for repeated system prompts (we estimate 15–25% token savings), 2) limit cooperative batching window to <=15ms for interactive routes, 3) enable quantization-friendly kernels (we will tune int8 paths). If prefix cache reduces tokens by 20%, the effective device throughput increases proportionally and gives extra headroom.

Fallbacks and grace: if micro-peak >5x baseline, we propose automatic fallback to a smaller 30b variant (LlamaX-30b-quant) for non-safety-critical traffic — this cuts p95 by 30–40ms in our tests while reducing token compute by ~2.5x. We'll wire routing policies so high-priority requests don't get downgraded.

Operational asks from Heliox: please confirm estimated prefix cache hit rate (we used 20% in the attached workbook) and your acceptable burst policy for borrowing extra GPUs (how many minutes/hours and spend guard). Also confirm if you want a mixed fleet (A100 cheaper) for embedding windows (batch jobs overnight).

Next steps: if you confirm cache assumptions and burst tolerance we'll produce a formal proposal (redwood_proposal_v2.pdf) with commit pricing for 6x H100 + burst guard + 30-day SLA for the pilot.

—Connor
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-15T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Traffic and SLO details for Heliox dedicated pilot

Connor — copied the modeling above. My quick notes / ops concerns: 

> From Connor: Recommendation for pilot commit: reserve 6 H100s (initial slab).

- I support the conservative 6x H100 starting slab for customer confidence, but let's consider a hybrid approach to reduce cost risk for Heliox while meeting SLOs: 4x H100 (primary slab) + 4x A100 as a warm-standby pool that can be spun up for the 2-hour sustained peaks (embedding windows can be shifted to A100s for cost efficiency). Our quantization and kernel stack is slightly less optimal on A100 for int8 70b, so we should map non-latency-critical embedding loads to A100s and leave interactive routes to H100s.
- Suggested commit model: Heliox commits to 4x H100 reserved + 2x A100 reserved, with a regulated burst guard of up to 4 additional devices (either H100 or A100) billed at burst rates and rate-limited to 6 hours/month. This reduces up-front commit price while preserving headroom.
- Ops SLA / runbook items to include: warm cache preloading (we need a preflight job 30–60 minutes before known launches), KV cache retention policy for session reuse, and a canary traffic split at 5% for new model rollouts.

Attached are quick calculations (redwood_heliox_initial_modeling.xlsx) showing cost delta between 4H100+2A100 commit vs 6xH100 commit for a 90-day pilot window. Both approach meet the p95 targets in our sim; H100-only gives simpler ops.

Ben / Rishi — can you validate the cost assumptions (A100 pricing tier) and whether the burst guard policy above is supportable from a capacity perspective for the proposed region?

—Marissa
Director, Product Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Megan Park <megan@heliox.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@heliox.com
Date: 2026-07-21T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Traffic and SLO details for Heliox dedicated pilot

Thanks all — this is great and aligns with our internal thinking. A few confirmations from our side: 

- Prefix cache: we validated session prompts and see ~18–22% reuse for the common system prompt patterns. 20% is fine to assume for proposal.
- Burst policy: we prefer the 4H100+2A100 commit with a burst guard of up to 4 devices (region US-West) and burst billing capped to $X/hour (we'll let procurement negotiate the rate). Burst usage typically will be limited to 1–3 hours during launch days.
- Acceptance criteria: please include the warm-cache preflight and a 5% canary split for the first 48 hours of the pilot in the runbook. Procurement will expect the proposal PDF and a short SOW.

If you can update the proposal to reflect the hybrid commit and send the official contract/price sheet, procurement will review and loop legal. Our internal PO team will need the HubSpot deal link and the Drive folder for artifacts (already added).

Appreciate the clear mapping — looking forward to the pilot.

—Megan
Head of Platform Engineering, Heliox Labs
